title: MAS runtime conformance report — the instrument registered before the runtime
description: What `benchmark/mas-conformance.ts` writes: the source and suite census, the registered positive/negative workflow fixtures with their oracles, the suite substrate probes executed against the published JarenJS primitives, and one integrated row per registration stating honestly how far the MAS runtime has come. Registration is immutable input — fixture ids, canonical revisions, expected outputs, ordered event/aggregation oracles, concurrency bounds, call/tool/context/restore counts, or one expected `{ code, path }` refusal — and its identity excludes every observation. Suite probes prove the substrate exists (`state: 'substrate'`); they never pass a MAS fixture. Integrated rows are replaced by id as the runtime lands; they never change the registration or its denominators. The counts reconcile by `$query` at validation time, the gate's live-call counters are literal zeros (a conformance run is keyless and clock-free by construction), and `reportId` is the canonical SHA-256 of the document with that field excluded.

source.description: HEAD, tree cleanliness and the ordered path/digest manifest of everything this instrument's behavior reads. Deterministic: no clock, no hostname, no absolute path.

registration.description: The immutable input layer: what the runtime will be judged against. Later orders replace integrated rows by id; they never change this block or its denominators.

suiteProbes.description: Direct executions of published JarenJS primitives with controlled promises and injected clocks. A probe passing says the substrate exists; it does not pass a MAS fixture and its state is never 'integrated'.

durability.description: Measurements over the real MAS store adapter and suite queue with injected clocks: transactional five-member node completion, activation compare-and-swap, semantic idempotency replay, namespaced segment checkpoints with atomic terminal prune, reclaim-closes-without-execution, and the uncertain-attempt guard. Durable-scripted persistence evidence — never a runtime fixture pass.

gate.description: A conformance run is keyless and offline by construction: the counters are literal zeros in the schema, so a report of a run that bought a live completion or reached a network cannot validate at all. Scripted calls are counted per integrated row; they are not live calls.

live.description: The optional live weekly-report row. Runtime conformance never depends on it — the claims are scheduler/contract/durability semantics and the scripted clients exercise the exact AI/tool/context seams — so without a separately planned and authorized spend it is the explicit value not-run with its reason, never an omission.

decision.description: The mechanical claim decision, computed AFTER the report identity so stating it cannot move its evidence address. `runtime-conformant` holds only when all seven clauses hold; the `$query` recomputation makes a forged outcome or a hidden failure schema-invalid.

validationCode.description: A reserved MAS validation refusal code. The validator that honors these arrives in a later order; the registration pins them first.

eventOracle.description: One expected durable lifecycle record, `<invocation path>:<status>` in expected commit order. Iterated or nested invocations carry their path segments (`refine/1/bump`).

aggregationOracle.description: The declared-order fan-in oracle for one target port: the ordered source invocation ids the aggregated message value must reflect, independent of completion timing.

concurrency.description: Expected bounds on maximumObservedConcurrency, measured by a counter incremented on handler entry and decremented in `finally` — never inferred from durations.

registeredFixture.description: One registered fixture as the report re-states it: identity, canonical source revision, the declared workflow version and the full oracle. The fixture file holds the workflow bytes and script; the registration identity excludes observations.

integratedRow.description: One row per registration, in registration order. `not-implemented` states the honest absence of a runtime with zero attempts and calls; `validated` says the workflow validated and planned without executing; `refused-as-registered` says a negative fixture refused at its exact registered code and pointer; `runtime-pass` says the full registered oracle held and requires workflow, registry and executable revisions.

agentTurn.description: One scripted provider reply for an agent node, in call order. A `toolCall` turn asks the runtime to execute the named tool; a `content` turn ends the loop or answers a normalization request. Usage is scripted so budget accounting is deterministic.

fixtureScript.description: The deterministic host plan the future runner binds: scripted pure task queries by invocation id, scripted agent reply sequences by invocation id, a concurrency gate driven by deferred promises (never wall-clock sleeps), one optional stop/reclaim point, one optional typed interaction response and one optional scripted failure site.

fixtureDocument.description: One committed fixture file: the proposed high-level workflow bytes (treated as data until the MAS package supplies its validator), the deterministic script and the exact oracle.

manifest.description: The ordered fixture manifest (`benchmark/fixtures/mas/manifest.json`): the shared registry and CONFIG catalog references and the 11 positive plus 7 negative registrations with their canonical source revisions, in registration order.
